question: What will be the highest 24-hour PSI reading recorded in any region of Singapore on September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: the current daily max is ~86 (C region, 9 Sep 01:00 SGT) and NEA has forecast 'Moderate - Low Unhealthy' unchanged for five consecutive advisories. At 9-10 days lead there is no day-specific skill for 18 Sep, so the estimate is the regime marginal, not a persistence extrapolation. Prior from the reference class (mid-Sept days inside an already-active SE Asian haze episode) is ~95; I hold the median just under that at 92 because 2026's fire load is Kalimantan-dominated (12,212 vs 3,440 Sumatra hotspots Jan-Aug), and Singapore's severe episodes are driven by South Sumatra peat, not Borneo. Two-sided: upside is a historic-strength El Nino with below-normal rainfall through November per ASMC, Sumatra fires peaking later than Kalimantan's, and southwesterly/southeasterly transport - hence a heavy right tail and 5% above 200. Downside is that the observed floor during this episode has still been ~85 daily max, so a drop below the mid-60s needs an actual wet spell plus wind shift; sub-40 is near-impossible with regional smoke loaded, hence 2%. Evidence is thin on 2026 Sumatra-specific fire trajectory and I found no prediction market pricing this, so I stay anchored near the class base rate rather than reading the episode's 116 peak as a trend.

calls.reasoning: The resolved quantity is a max over ~5 regions x 24 hourly publications, which runs materially above the single-hour ranges NEA quotes in evening advisories - the key correction across the three runs. On the primary hourly series, 2026 daily maxima ran 76-123 from Aug 20 to Sep 8, with the last three days at 93/97/83: elevated and intact, not receded. At 10 days lead there is no day-specific skill, so 18 Sep is a draw from the regime distribution with modest seasonal upward tilt (Sumatra fires peak later than Kalimantan's; mid-to-late Sep is the peak Singapore-impact window; monsoon-transition relief arrives ~October). Offsetting: the season's hotspot load is Kalimantan-dominated and vents mainly to Sarawak/Peninsular Malaysia, plumes were observed drifting northwards, and the season ceiling is 123 with no 2015-style escalation demonstrated. Median 95 - roughly a 60/40 that the day stays inside Moderate - with a heavy right tail and 5% above 200 for a south-Sumatra peat outbreak under sustained southerly flow. No p_below_lower: a clean wet-season day still printed max-region 62.
calls.reconciliation: The decisive dispute was factual and about the instrument, not about judgment: Runs 1 and 2 anchored their centre on NEA's 6pm advisory ranges (Sep 8: '62-74'), while Run 3 retrieved the data.gov.sg hourly PSI API and reported true daily maxima across all regions and hours (Sep 8: 83; Sep 4-5: 123). Since the question resolves off exactly that max-over-regions-and-hours, Run 3's series is the correct measurement of the resolved quantity and Run 2's centre of 82 is biased low by roughly ten points. Run 2's cited Malay Mail figure (central 123 at 1am, 5 Sep) independently corroborates the API series, and it also settles Run 1's lower 116 episode peak in favour of 123. Correcting this also overturns Run 2's 'already receded' reading: Sep 6-8 maxima of 93/97/83 sit above the late-August baseline of 76-78, so the regime is elevated and intact. In the other direction I discounted Run 3's reliance on the 2019 same-date analogue - one year is one draw, and 2019's fire load was Sumatra-weighted where 2026's is Kalimantan-weighted, which all three runs agree transports to Singapore less efficiently. That leaves genuine but modest seasonal upward drift (Sumatra peaks later than Kalimantan, mid-to-late September is the peak impact window, relief historically arrives with the October monsoon transition), giving a median of 95 - above Run 2's corrected level, below Run 3's analogue-driven 102. I adopted Run 3's omission of p_below_lower on factual grounds: its primary-source clean-day data point (max-region 62 on 15 Jan 2026) shows sub-40 has no mechanism, so Runs 1 and 2's 2% is unsupported. All three runs converged at 5% for the >200 tail and I carried that forward. The hotspot-count contradiction (14,000-23,000/day vs 946 nationwide) could not be settled without retrieval and is left carrying its uncertainty; it does not drive the estimate, which rests on the observed PSI series. Reference class and dispersion basis are my own, informed by the reconciled series: the within-2026-regime 10-90 width is only ~47 points, but at 10 days lead regime uncertainty dominates, so I state 82 from the haze-active-September class SD, consistent with 2019's ~80-point mid-September spread. No web access this run, so 'sources' is empty.
